Absolute Value Equations

What You’ll Learn

Section titled “What You’ll Learn”

In this lesson you’ll learn what absolute value means and how to solve simple absolute value equations.

The Concept

Section titled “The Concept”

Absolute value ∣x∣|x|∣x∣ is the distance from 0 on a number line — always positive or zero.

∣x∣=5|x| = 5∣x∣=5 means x=5x = 5x=5 or x=−5x = -5x=−5 (two solutions).

Solving ∣expression∣=number|\text{expression}| = \text{number}∣expression∣=number

  1. Set up two cases: expression =number= \text{number}=number or expression =−number= -\text{number}=−number
  2. Solve each equation separately.

Example: ∣x+3∣=7|x + 3| = 7∣x+3∣=7

x+3=7x+3=−7x=4x=−10\begin{aligned} x + 3 &= 7 & x + 3 &= {-}7 \\ x &= 4 & x &= {-}10 \end{aligned}x+3x​=7=4​x+3x​=−7=−10​

Solutions: x=4x = 4x=4 or x=−10x = -10x=−10

Check: ∣4+3∣=∣7∣=7|4 + 3| = |7| = 7∣4+3∣=∣7∣=7 ✓ and ∣−10+3∣=∣−7∣=7|-10 + 3| = |-7| = 7∣−10+3∣=∣−7∣=7 ✓

Note: If ∣expression∣=negative number|\text{expression}| = \text{negative number}∣expression∣=negative number → no solution (absolute value can’t be negative).

Worked Examples

Section titled “Worked Examples”

Solve ∣2x−4∣=10|2x - 4| = 10∣2x−4∣=10

Case 1:

2x−4=102x=14x=7\begin{aligned} 2x - 4 &= 10 \\ 2x &= 14 \\ x &= 7 \end{aligned}2x−42xx​=10=14=7​

Case 2:

2x−4=−102x=−6x=−3\begin{aligned} 2x - 4 &= {-}10 \\ 2x &= {-}6 \\ x &= {-}3 \end{aligned}2x−42xx​=−10=−6=−3​

Check: ∣2(7)−4∣=∣14−4∣=10|2(7) - 4| = |14 - 4| = 10∣2(7)−4∣=∣14−4∣=10 ✓ and ∣2(−3)−4∣=∣−6−4∣=∣−10∣=10|2(-3) - 4| = |-6 - 4| = |-10| = 10∣2(−3)−4∣=∣−6−4∣=∣−10∣=10 ✓

Real-World Applications

Section titled “Real-World Applications”

Absolute value represents distances or differences without direction:

  • Temperature 5 degrees from target: ∣t−72∣=5|t - 72| = 5∣t−72∣=5 → t=77t = 77t=77 or t=67t = 67t=67
  • Budget overrun/underrun: ∣spent−budget∣≤20|\text{spent} - \text{budget}| \leq 20∣spent−budget∣≤20 dollars
  • Error tolerance: ∣measurement−true value∣<0.05|\text{measurement} - \text{true value}| < 0.05∣measurement−true value∣<0.05

These help with tolerances, errors, or ranges in measurements and finance.

You’ve Got This

Absolute value means “distance from zero” — so equations have two solutions (positive and negative directions). Set up both cases, solve, and always check both answers. Practice with distances or budgets — it makes sense quickly.
